results.name: trial_index_yes_slope
results.description: OLS slope of rating on trial_index, in change of yes-probability per 100 trials; t_observed above null_mean (~0) means people drift toward saying yes more over the session, which the stationary model cannot produce (below = drift toward no).

results.name: single_example_same_decade_other_digit_yes
results.description: In single-example sets, yes rate for targets in the same decade (t//10 == x//10) as the example but with a different final digit; t_observed above null_mean means people generalize within a decade more than the model (digit similarity + band) predicts; below means the model over-produces same-decade yeses.
results.code:
# name: single_example_same_decade_other_digit_yes
# description: In single-example sets, yes rate for targets in the same decade (t//10 == x//10) as the example but with a different final digit; t_observed above null_mean means people generalize within a decade more than the model (digit similarity + band) predicts; below means the model over-produces same-decade yeses.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",")
    x = pd.to_numeric(s.where(single, "0"), errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    m = single.values & (t // 10 == x // 10) & (t % 10 != x % 10)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float).values[m].mean())

results.name: set_yes_rate_dispersion
results.description: SD across number_sets of the set-level yes rate (targets that are not examples); t_observed above null_mean means generalization breadth differs more between sets (some nearly all-no, others nearly all-yes) than the model's features produce; below means the model over-differentiates sets.
results.code:
# name: set_yes_rate_dispersion
# description: SD across number_sets of the set-level yes rate (targets that are not examples); t_observed above null_mean means generalization breadth differs more between sets (some nearly all-no, others nearly all-yes) than the model's features produce; below means the model over-differentiates sets.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    in_set = np.array([v in [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s, v in zip(sets, t)])
    d = df.loc[~in_set]
    rates = d.groupby("number_set")["rating"].mean()
    if len(rates) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(rates.std())

results.name: mixed_parity_set_unmatched_digit_yes
results.description: In sets containing both odd and even examples, yes rate for targets whose final digit matches no example (not examples); t_observed above null_mean means people treat parity-mixed sets as a broad "any number" category more than the model's averaged parity credit predicts; below means the model over-generalizes in mixed sets.

results.name: above_vs_below_range_unmatched_gap
results.description: In multi-example sets, among targets matching no example's final digit and outside [min,max] of the examples, yes rate for targets above the max minus targets below the min; t_observed above null_mean means people extrapolate upward more than downward (a magnitude asymmetry the symmetric decade-band term cannot produce); below means downward extrapolation is favoured.
results.code:
# name: above_vs_below_range_unmatched_gap
# description: In multi-example sets, among targets matching no example's final digit and outside [min,max] of the examples, yes rate for targets above the max minus targets below the min; t_observed above null_mean means people extrapolate upward more than downward (a magnitude asymmetry the symmetric decade-band term cannot produce); below means downward extrapolation is favoured.
def test_statistic(df):
    info = {}
    for s in df["number_set"].astype(str).unique():
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        info[s] = (len(xs) >= 2, min(xs), max(xs), set(x % 10 for x in xs))
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    multi = np.array([info[s][0] for s in sets])
    lo = np.array([info[s][1] for s in sets])
    hi = np.array([info[s][2] for s in sets])
    unm = np.array([(v % 10) not in info[s][3] for s, v in zip(sets, t)])
    a = multi & unm & (t > hi)
    b = multi & unm & (t < lo)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: modal_vs_minority_digit_match_gap
results.description: In sets of >=3 examples where a final digit is shared by >=2 but not all examples, yes rate for targets ending in that modal digit minus yes rate for targets ending in a minority (single-example) digit (targets not examples); t_observed above null_mean means people adopt the majority "ends in d" rule and discount outlier examples more than the model's proportional digit averaging; below means less.
results.code:
# name: modal_vs_minority_digit_match_gap
# description: In sets of >=3 examples where a final digit is shared by >=2 but not all examples, yes rate for targets ending in that modal digit minus yes rate for targets ending in a minority (single-example) digit (targets not examples); t_observed above null_mean means people adopt the majority "ends in d" rule and discount outlier examples more than the model's proportional digit averaging; below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    info = {}
    for s in df["number_set"].astype(str).unique():
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        ds = [x % 10 for x in xs]
        cnt = {d: ds.count(d) for d in ds}
        mx = max(cnt.values())
        ok = len(xs) >= 3 and mx >= 2 and mx < len(xs)
        modal = set(d for d, c in cnt.items() if c == mx)
        minor = set(d for d, c in cnt.items() if c == 1)
        info[s] = (ok, modal, minor, set(xs))
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    base = np.array([info[s][0] and (v not in info[s][3]) for s, v in zip(sets, t)])
    a = base & np.array([(v % 10) in info[s][1] for s, v in zip(sets, t)])
    b = base & np.array([(v % 10) in info[s][2] for s, v in zip(sets, t)])
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: parity_only_credit_odd_minus_even_sets
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples that share one parity but do NOT all share a final digit, yes rate for same-parity targets matching no example's final digit (not examples), all-odd sets minus all-even sets; t_observed above null_mean means people give odd-number sets more parity generalization than even sets (the model treats parity symmetrically), below means even sets get more.
results.code:
# name: parity_only_credit_odd_minus_even_sets
# description: Among sets of >=2 examples that share one parity but do NOT all share a final digit, yes rate for same-parity targets matching no example's final digit (not examples), all-odd sets minus all-even sets; t_observed above null_mean means people give odd-number sets more parity generalization than even sets (the model treats parity symmetrically), below means even sets get more.
def test_statistic(df):
    info = {}
    for s in df["number_set"].astype(str).unique():
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        par = set(x % 2 for x in xs)
        dig = set(x % 10 for x in xs)
        ok = len(xs) >= 2 and len(par) == 1 and len(dig) > 1
        info[s] = (ok, xs[0] % 2, dig, set(xs))
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    sel = np.array([info[s][0] and v % 2 == info[s][1] and (v % 10 not in info[s][2]) and (v not in info[s][3]) for s, v in zip(sets, t)])
    odd = np.array([info[s][1] == 1 for s in sets])
    a = sel & odd
    b = sel & ~odd
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: power_of_two_target_advantage
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples that are all powers of 2, yes rate for power-of-2 targets minus yes rate for other even targets (targets not examples); t_observed above null_mean means people infer a "powers of 2" rule the model (final digit + common-factor multiples) under-produces; below means the model over-favours powers of 2.
